findings.title: Authorization behavior was mischaracterized: anonymous item-image reads are not rejected by item visibility
findings.resolution: Corrected in all touched files. docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md section 3.3 and section 4.4, docs/changelog.md, README.md, PLANS.md Task 5.1 status, and docs/implementation/5.1/worker-report.json now state that the GET/HEAD read actions carry no [Authorize] and resolve via GetItemById<BaseItem>(itemId, User.GetUserId()); an anonymous empty user id maps to a null user, ItemIsVisible(item, null) returns true for any non-null item, so a known item's image is served anonymously (HTTP 200) and only an unknown id / missing image yields 404. The retained guidance is that later tasks must not assume a 401 or treat the route as an authorization boundary. The worker-report live-probe note explicitly attributes the 404 to the unknown item id rather than visibility rejection. Re-verified against pinned source and OpenAPI; no contradictory wording remains.
evidence: README.md Phase 5 entry (route/authorization status live-confirmed; cache/resize from source).
worker-report.json summary, validation item 15, known_limitations item 43.

Pinned source: ImageController.cs read actions have no [Authorize]; ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.GetUserId() -> default(Guid); LibraryManager.GetItemById<T>(Guid, Guid) -> null user; LibraryManager.ItemIsVisible(item, null) -> true; OpenAPI security=null.

findings.title: README/changelog overstated live confirmation of the cache-header and never-upscale resize behavior
findings.resolution: Corrected. README.md and docs/changelog.md now label the image-tag/ETag/Last-Modified/cache-header behavior and never-upscale resize path as confirmed from the pinned source/artifact, and reserve live-confirmed for the route/authorization status observations and OpenAPI security metadata. worker-report.json records the same distinction. The research document section 3.3 already labeled only the status observations live-confirmed.
evidence: README.md lines ~182-188: 'Jellyfin's image-tag/ETag/Last-Modified and cache-header behavior and its never-upscale resize path are confirmed from the pinned source/artifact.'
docs/changelog.md: '- Delivery behavior (confirmed from the pinned source/artifact)' and authorization bullet '(route/status observations live-confirmed; pinned OpenAPI shows security=null ...)'.

findings.title: [Route] decoration wording was imprecise relative to the inherited base route
findings.resolution: Corrected. docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md section 3.1 now states that ImageController directly declares [Route("")], that BaseJellyfinApiController declares [Route("[controller]")] and RouteAttribute.Inherited is true, and that the controller's own [Route("")] overrides the inherited prefix so the effective paths are the root-relative templates listed. Consistent with the pinned OpenAPI, which has no /Image/... paths.
evidence: BaseJellyfinApiController.cs line 13 [Route("[controller]")]; ImageController.cs line 42 [Route("")]; RouteAttribute.Inherited == true; OpenAPI has no /Image/... paths.
